data.title: Kantor citizenship case widens to heirs, businesses
data.description: An investigation is under way to determine whether the heirs and business interests of Jewish community leader Yosef Chaim Kantor have breached any laws following the revocation of his Thai citizenship, Deputy Interior Minister Polapee Suwunchwee said yesterday.

data.title: Karon named 'disaster area' after heavy downpours
data.description: Phuket has declared parts of Muang district a disaster-hit area after heavy rain and strong winds caused flooding and mudslides.

data.title: Arnon and four others     jailed for royal defamation
data.description: The Criminal Court has sentenced lawyer and protest leader Arnon Nampa and four co-defendants to two years and eight months in prison each for royal defamation, without suspension.

data.title: Agencies told to join graft reform
data.description: At least 12 government agencies will join an initiative to improve transparency, combat corruption and reform public administration.

data.title: Police raid nominee businesses
data.description: Provincial Police Region 8 and provincial authorities raided five locations in Krabi's Muang district on Thursday, arresting 28 people over alleged nominee business operations and seizing assets worth about 88 million baht for examination.

data.title: A Greek classic
data.description: Greek composer, vocalist, lyricist and ensemble leader Stella Papalamprou is riding high in the World Music charts with her latest release Protanixin, a six-track self-released album that explores the music of the Pontic region in Greek Macedonia.

data.title: Road  to WorldPride 2030
data.description: Bangkok Pride recently launched its official bidding book for WorldPride 2030. The event, which took place at the Bangkok Arts and Cultural Centre, revealed how Thailand would bid to host WorldPride.

data.title: 2nd UOB Wonder Lab a hit with competitors
data.description: UOB Thailand has officially concluded the second edition of its signature Wonder Lab initiative, honouring three standout youth teams for their visionary approaches to sustainability communications.

data.title: Cultivating classics between classes
data.description: Inspirational music-making of the most heartwarmingly collaborative variety was on full display recently at the latest Sounds Of Wireless series performance, presented by the combined talents of the Royal Bangkok Symphony School (RBSS) and the truly exceptional Immanuel Orchestra, a charitable music education project which provides free string instrument tuition for under-privileged boys and girls from one of Bangkok's poorest districts, Klong Toey.

data.title: Hudson's King's Cup plans hit by club snub
data.description: National football team head coach Anthony Hudson is forced to rethink his plans after several Thai League 1 clubs refused to release their players for next month's King's Cup tournament, which will take place in Sri Sa Ket province from Nov 14-17.

data.title: Cod Army revel, Kane joins the royalty
data.description: The fundamental appeal of Cup competitions in football is that every now and again there is a major upset. And that is exactly what happened in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night when League Two strugglers Fleetwood Town beat Premier League defending champions Arsenal 5-3 on penalties after the score was 1-1 in regular time.

data.title: Fatima tones it down
data.description: Opera in Thai is a challenging prospect. In addition to handling the aspects of choosing a librettist, creating an effective operatic structure and writing for that most finicky of instruments, the human voice, a composer has to deal with the Thai language.

data.title: Your daily horoscope for Oct 31
data.description: The day of the week you were born on can reveal a lot... Read on. ✨= today's motto,⏰ = work, ₿ = money, ❤️= taken, ⚤ = single

data.title: Dems say 'no' to debate without vote
data.description: The Democrat Party has ruled out a separate parliamentary debate without a vote under Section 152, saying the opposition should focus on its planned no-confidence motion.

data.title: First-half blitz in HK earns Rabbits their first victory
data.description: BG Pathum United claimed their first win of their AFC Champions League Two campaign when they defeated Tai Po 3-0 at Mong Kok Stadium in Hong Kong on Thursday night.

data.title: Govt plans 'nightlife sandbox' for Khao San, Rambuttri
data.description: The government plans to introduce a sandbox scheme covering Khao San and Rambuttri roads in Bangkok to improve law enforcement at entertainment venues and prevent corruption among state officials.

data.title: Lifetime driving licences 'won't be binned'
data.description: The Department of Land Transport (DLT) has dismissed social media reports that it plans to cancel or confiscate lifetime driving licences, insisting that existing holders can continue using them legally.

data.title: Govt braces for US-Iran fallout
data.description: The National Security Council (NSC) will convene an urgent meeting on Wednesday to review national preparedness measures amid growing concerns over the situation in the Middle East.

data.title: Influencer seeks foundation probe
data.description: A Facebook influencer has filed a police complaint seeking an investigation into the Good Deeds Foundation over allegations that it used public donations for purposes unrelated to its charitable objectives.

data.title: Trump, Milei under pressure to explain Bolsonaro flight from Brazil
data.description: BRASíLIA - US President Donald Trump and Argentina's Javier Milei faced mounting pressure Friday to explain the role their countries played in helping Flavio Bolsonaro flee Brazil after he had his passports cancelled.

data.title: Polish riot police deployed after court chief suspended
data.description: WARSAW - Riot police deployed around Poland's constitutional court and President Karol Nawrocki called off an African visit on Friday after the suspension of its chief justice in a battle between the centrist government and the nationalist right.

data.title: France fears new street violence at Halloween protests
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Shops and businesses in Paris and other French cities on Friday boarded up windows amid fears of fresh street violence during a third consecutive weekend of protests -- this time clashing with Halloween.

data.title: British king reflects on colonial atrocities in Guyana
data.description: GEORGETOWN (GUYANA) - Britain's King Charles paid homage to fallen soldiers and reflected on colonial atrocities in Guyana during a whistle-stop tour of the former colony on Friday.
